title: What they said at the time

clips.q: This should turn the toy business on its ear.
clips.who: **Kurt Barnard**, retail consultant, on the sale to Consolidated Stores, Los Angeles Times, Mar 26, 1996[^8]

clips.q: We never get depressed around here because we can always come play with the toys.
clips.who: **Michael Glazer**, chief executive, four months after the buyout, Apr 19, 2001[^15]

clips.q: Consolidated never believed that Wall Street gave them the value for KB they thought it deserved in the marketplace.
I just think that KB Toys is in a death spiral.
clips.who: **C. Britt Beemer**, America’s Research Group, The Washington Post, Nov 3, 2007[^22]

clips.q: There were a lot of tears.
clips.who: **Nancy Moffett**, a KB employee for more than 18 years, on the morning of the second filing, The Berkshire Eagle, Dec 12, 2008[^24]

clips.q: Toys are recession-resistant; they’re not recession-proof.
clips.who: **Gerrick Johnson**, BMO Capital Markets, Los Angeles Times, Dec 12, 2008[^23]

clips.q: Their business model was obsolete. The world had changed. KB had not changed.
clips.who: **Jim Silver**, Time to Play magazine, to PolitiFact, Jan 13, 2012[^27]

clips.q: In hindsight, it’s possible that Bain may have taken a dividend on KB Toys that was too aggressive.
clips.who: **Roger Goddu**, former Toys “R” Us president and later a KB investor and consultant, to PolitiFact, Jan 13, 2012[^27]

clips.q: Once we get the money together we will be off and running.
clips.who: **Ellia Kassoff**, Strategic Marks, as quoted by The Toy Book, Mar 15, 2019[^33]
